details: Eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August, marking the highest level in nearly three years. This surge is largely attributed to escalating energy prices, fueled by renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. With the European Central Bank's Governing Council meeting on September 10, markets are heavily anticipating another interest rate increase to combat inflation that remains stubbornly above the 2% target.
title: ECB Poised for September Rate Hike Amid Soaring Eurozone Inflation

details: Government borrowing costs worldwide have surged, with UK 10-year gilt yields reaching their highest levels since 2008. This global bond sell-off is driven by heightened inflation concerns, exacerbated by intensifying US-Iran tensions which have pushed Brent crude oil prices near $97 a barrel. The rising yields reflect market expectations of continued monetary tightening by central banks to curb inflationary pressures.
title: Global Bond Market Sell-off Intensifies as Oil Prices Climb

details: Bank of Japan board member Hajime Takata has called for agile interest rate adjustments to effectively counter intensifying inflationary pressures. He suggested the BOJ should react flexibly to economic developments, moving away from a predetermined pace of rate hikes. This hawkish stance indicates a potential pivot towards more aggressive monetary tightening in Japan, marking 2026 as a pivotal year for the central bank's policy.
title: BOJ Board Member Advocates for Flexible Rate Hikes
